pull.title: validation: check the most recent AssumeUTXO commitment during IBD
pull.body:
**Problem:** AssumeUTXO verifies imported UTXOs against a hash we bake into the binary.
Every node reconstructs the same UTXO set during ordinary IBD, but [does not check its hash against the existing AssumeUTXO commitment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32377).

**Fix:** During ordinary block validation, verify the provided AssumeUTXO hash when block connection reaches the corresponding block, stopping the node on a mismatch.
Flush pending changes to disk before hashing the UTXO set and comparing the result with the commitment.

Keep only the latest AssumeUTXO commitment per network to limit the extra hashing work during IBD, and update the release process to replace it.
Users who need older snapshots for research or other purposes can use a compatible older release or restore the corresponding commitment as `m_assumeutxo_data` and recompile.

Persist block-index test edits before reloading to prepare for the IBD check's forced flush.
Check that an unrelated chain passes the fixture's commitment height without starting a UTXO scan.
Check that interrupted snapshot validation leaves the snapshot unvalidated and can be retried.

validation: verify the provided AssumeUTXO hash

Verify the provided AssumeUTXO hash when block connection reaches the corresponding block.
Skip other chains at the same height.
This checks the developer-provided commitment against the UTXO set that every node reconstructs during IBD (see #32377).
Reuse the AssumeUTXO background verifier and its reporting.
Flush pending UTXO changes to disk before hashing the set.
Stop on a flush failure before updating the tip or mempool.
Request shutdown if UTXO statistics cannot be computed or the commitment does not match, preserving normal shutdown interruptions.
AssumeUTXO import verification and background validation remain mandatory.

`MaybeValidateSnapshot()` already invalidates a failed snapshot and requests shutdown, but `ConnectTip()` reports success to its caller.

Keep interrupted hashing distinct so normal shutdown does not become a validation failure.

<sub>Task `iwyu`: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/38744710504/job/116455202409</sub>
<sub>LLM reason (✨ experimental): CI failed because the IWYU check modified `src/kernel/chainparams.cpp` by removing an unused `cassert` include, leaving an uncommitted diff.</sub>

<details><summary>Hints</summary>

Try to run the tests locally, according to the documentation. However, a CI failure may still
happen due to a number of reasons, for example:

* Possibly due to a silent merge conflict (the changes in this pull request being
incompatible with the current code in the target branch). If so, make sure to rebase on the latest
commit of the target branch.

* A sanitizer issue, which can only be found by compiling with the sanitizer and running the
  affected test.

* An intermittent issue.

Leave a comment here, if you need help tracking down a confusing failure.

</details>

Concept ACK, see #32377, with two caveats: 

> stopping the node on a mismatch

I think this risks introducing a new effective checkpoint. If the snapshot were malicious, normal users couldn't sync and a subset may decide to restart in AssumeUTXO mode.

It seems better to emit a warning, severe enough that the GUI shows it, but not aborting. It's a clear sign there's something wrong with the software. Even though it doesn't affect them, they should seek advice, since it's a giant red flag.

(in such a malicious scenario, developers would presumably change the warning to an error, exactly to achieve this wrong behavior)

This was already discussed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32377#issuecomment-2851372290, but the implementation doesn't match the conclusion there.

> Keep only the latest AssumeUTXO commitment per network to limit the extra hashing work during IBD

Maybe limit the scope of this PR by only _checking_ the latest hash, but not (yet) deleting the other hashes.

---

You mentioned offline that the performance impact of this extra check is minimal. It would be good to provide some numbers in the PR description.

I'm not up to speed on how often and when we flush the chainstate to disk during IBD nowadays. How does this interact with that?

Concept ACK

As there is a hash provided that requires trust, the more checks the better. It makes sense to use all nodes performing IBD to also perform this check, as it's relatively cheap to do.

> It seems better to emit a warning, severe enough that the GUI shows it, but not aborting.

Two suggestions:

- Introduce an option to skip the new AssumeUTXO hash check (may be a hidden option) -- useful in itself.
- In the unlikely case a hash mismatch is found, abort, and advice the user to shout out and restart with the ignore AssumeUTXO hash check option. That way the effect is hard to ignore by the user, but easy to bypass.

> Maybe limit the scope of this PR by only _checking_ the latest hash, but not (yet) deleting the other hashes.

For clarity it's worth mentioning that the latest hash a user is checking may not be the same as the latest hash of the latest release, nor the one used by most nodes in the network. (For the sake of example, assuming v35 has been released, and a majority of the network is on v34, when a user is running v33, the checked hash will not match the hash used by many other nodes.) Note that it would be desirable to check the hash of newer versions, but of course it's not possible to hardcode hashes of future releases in the source code. So not checking the non-latest hashes is fine, but it's useful to keep them for visibility.

What's the performance impact when hitting such a block?

Doesn't this make the result of a release including bad snaphot data worse for everyone -- Alice who does IBD has her node crash despite having good data that she fully verified, and Bob who uses the bad snapshot still potentially fails to an incorrect chain unless Alice has already done her IBD run and Bob happens to hear Alice complain about the failure?

Having predictable snapshot points (every 14112 blocks [per bip452](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2137/files)) would allow every node to calculate the appropriate hash (in the background on a leveldb snapshot without cs_main held, hopefully) and remember it, prior to a new release being considered, making verification much easier, and consistent across implementations. Including the block's muhash in the assumeutxo set would also probably work here, since muhash is already calculated and stored in coinstatsindex.

Concept ACK

One issue should be fixed before merge: a node that fails the new check aborts on an assertion, and a plain restart then syncs past the commitment without checking it again. I built 97b2138e39 with one digit of the regtest commitment's hash at height 299 changed, and let it sync the `feature_assumeutxo.py` chain to 310 from an unmodified node. In nine runs out of nine it logged the mismatch and the fatal error, then died with SIGABRT on `Assertion failed: (hashPrevBlock == view.GetBestBlock())` in `ConnectBlock`. Restarted with no new option, it starts at 299, syncs to 310 and never hashes the UTXO set again. `-reindex-chainstate` stops it once more, and a plain restart then syncs past 299 again. The same change on cce32b1687 syncs to 310. I can share the harness.

In `ConnectTip`, block 299 reaches the coins cache and the disk before the check, and the failure returns before `m_chain.SetTip`. The coins are at 299 while the chain stays at 298. Connecting 299 again, when the next block arrives during shutdown, trips the assert. The next start takes its tip from the coins. Moving the check after `UpdateTip` is not enough: on regtest the node then aborts in `CheckBlockIndex` instead. The unit test processes no block after the mismatch, so it reaches neither assert.

On warning versus stopping (Sjors, ajtowns): as it stands, the stop lasts only until the next restart.
